dialogue.content: 本日はよろしくお願いいたします
dialogue.English: Thank you for meeting with me today.

dialogue.content: おはようございます。よろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Good morning. I look forward to working with you today.

dialogue.content: 少し早いですがご準備がよろしければ始めても大丈夫ですか？
dialogue.English: We're a little early, but if you're ready, shall we begin?

dialogue.content: はい。お願いいたします
dialogue.English: Yes, please.

dialogue.content: お願いします。相談員です。今日はどのようなご相談ですか？
dialogue.English: Alright. I'm your counselor. What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: 勉強のことで困っています
dialogue.English: I’m having trouble with my studies.

dialogue.content: 勉強でお困りなのですね・・どのような状態なのか教えてもらえますか？
dialogue.English: I see you're struggling with your studies... Could you tell me more about what's going on?

dialogue.content: テストの点があまりよくなくて、親にすごく怒られてしまいます
dialogue.English: My test scores aren’t very good, and my parents get really angry with me.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、、それは辛いですね。親さんはどのように怒るんですか？
dialogue.English: I see... That must be tough. How do your parents express their anger?

dialogue.content: もっと勉強しなさいとよく言われます
dialogue.English: They often tell me to study more.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 勉強してるんですけど、それでも勉強しなさいと言います
dialogue.English: I am studying, but they still tell me to study more.

dialogue.content: はい、頑張ってるのにって思いますよね・・
dialogue.English: Yes, you must feel like, 'But I'm already trying so hard...'

dialogue.content: そうなんです…
dialogue.English: Exactly...

dialogue.content: お名前は何とお呼びしていいですか？
dialogue.English: What would you like me to call you?

dialogue.content: 神田です
dialogue.English: Kanda.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。ちなみに神田さんはおいくつか教えてもらっていいですか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. May I ask how old you are, Kanda?

dialogue.content: 14歳です
１４歳ですね。中学２年生ですか？
dialogue.English: Fourteen, I see. Are you in your second year of junior high?

dialogue.content: 中3です
dialogue.English: I’m in my third year of junior high.

dialogue.content: 失礼しました。中三なんですね。親さんとはお母さんお父さん、どちらが怒るんですか？
dialogue.English: My apologies. So you're in your third year. Which parent gets angry, your mother or your father?

dialogue.content: すごく言われるのは母です。父もたまに言います
dialogue.English: It's mostly my mother. My father says it sometimes too.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、両方だけど特にお母さんなんですね、、。言われて何か言い返したりしますか？
dialogue.English: I see, so both of them, but especially your mother. Do you ever talk back?

dialogue.content: 面倒なんで言い返さないようにしてます
dialogue.English: It’s a hassle, so I try not to talk back.

dialogue.content: もう面倒って思うくらいうるさいと思ってるんですよね
dialogue.English: It sounds like it feels so nagging that you find it a hassle to respond, right?

dialogue.content: そうですね。見張られている感じがするんです
dialogue.English: That's right. I feel like I'm being watched.

dialogue.content: そうですよね見張られてる感はほんっと窮屈ですよね。例えばどんな時にどんな事を言われますか？
dialogue.English: I can imagine. Feeling watched must be really suffocating. For example, what kinds of things do they say, and in what situations?

dialogue.content: 今回はテストが悪かったので、勉強が足りないとかどうしてできないの？とかそんなことです
dialogue.English: This time my test was bad, so they said things like, “You’re not studying enough,” or “Why can’t you do it?”

dialogue.content: 主にテストの結果が出た時に勉強の足りなさをくどくどって感じですね？
dialogue.English: So it's mainly when you get your test results back that they harp on about you not studying enough, is that right?

dialogue.content: いつも言われます。ただ、今回はテストがあったから結果のことでいろいろと言ってきました
dialogue.English: They say it all the time. But this time, because there was a test, they said various things about the results.

dialogue.content: いつもなんですね、それは嫌ですね。色々とは勉強について色々なのかな？
dialogue.English: So it’s all the time—that’s unpleasant. By “various things,” do you mean various things about studying?

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: Yes, that's right.

dialogue.content: 勉強って頑張ってるのにもっと成績あげろっていわれても困りますよね、、。勉強のやり方とかこうしろ、ああしろなんて言われますか？
dialogue.English: It must be difficult to be told to get better grades when you're already trying your best. Do they tell you how to study, like 'do this' or 'do that'?

dialogue.content: 塾にはいってます。今回、勉強のことでどうしたら成績がよくなるか相談したいんです
dialogue.English: I go to a cram school. This time, I want to talk about what I can do to improve my grades.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね・・神田さん自信で相談してみようと考えたりされたんですね。
dialogue.English: I see... So you decided on your own to seek advice.

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 自分でも困っているので
dialogue.English: Because I'm struggling with it myself.

dialogue.content: そうですよね、困ってることをお母さんに先先言われるから面倒と感じてるんですよね。
dialogue.English: Right. You feel it's a hassle because your mother brings up the very thing you're already struggling with.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ちなみにお母さんに見張られてる感じがすると言われましたが、勉強以外は大丈夫ですか？
dialogue.English: By the way, you mentioned feeling watched by your mother—apart from studying, is everything else okay?

dialogue.content: そこは特に感じません
dialogue.English: I don't particularly feel that way about other things.

dialogue.content: 三年生だから勉強はしないといけないけど、神田さんはお母さんにどのようになって欲しいとかありますか？
dialogue.English: Since you're in your third year, you do have to study, but is there anything you'd like your mother to do differently?

dialogue.content: お母さんですか？特になにも。
dialogue.English: My mother? Nothing in particular.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、では、ここまでの話を整理してもいいですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Then, may I summarize what we’ve discussed so far?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 神田さんは中学３年生で、自分でも成績が良くなくて困ってはいる。分かってるけどどうしたらよくなるかも分からないのにお母さんにテストの結果がでる度、いつもだけど、怒られる。
dialogue.English: You're Kanda, a third-year junior high student, and you're struggling because your grades aren't good. You know this, but you don't know how to improve, and yet your mother scolds you every time you get test results—which, as you said, is all the time.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: なんで、どうして、こんな成績なのと、見張られてる感じで苦しくなってここに来られました。
dialogue.English: You feel distressed from being watched and constantly asked, “Why are your grades like this?” and that's why you came here.

dialogue.content: でもお母さんの重圧や苦しい中自分でどうしたら成績伸びるんだろうと考えられました。
dialogue.English: But amidst the pressure from your mother and your distress, you've been thinking on your own about how you can improve your grades.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 塾で先生に相談してみようと思いつかれたのは、ほんっと凄い事だと思いました。面倒と言いながらちゃんとお母さんの言葉を考えられた事、前進されてるなって感じたのですがいかがですか？
dialogue.English: I think it's really amazing that you thought of consulting your teacher at cram school. And even while saying it's a hassle, you've properly considered your mother's words. I feel like you're making progress. What do you think?

dialogue.content: ちょっと違います。塾に相談ではなく、今日ここに相談しにきたんです
dialogue.English: Not exactly. I didn't come to consult the cram school; I came here today to get advice.

dialogue.content: 母は何も変わっていません
dialogue.English: My mother hasn’t changed at all.

dialogue.content: 失礼しました、塾ではなく、ここでどうしたらって事でしたか。一緒に考えましょうか・・
dialogue.English: I apologize. It wasn't about the cram school, but about what to do, right here. Shall we think about it together?

dialogue.content: 今回、勉強のことでどうしたら成績がよくなるか相談したいんですといいました
dialogue.English: I said that I want to talk about what I can do to improve my grades.

dialogue.content: そうですね、失礼しました。成績が良くなるにはどうしたらいいか？今勘違いしましたが、塾の先生に相談されるのも、神田さんの現状を一番しっているかと思うので良いかとは思いますが、どう思いますか？
dialogue.English: You're right, I apologize. The question is how to improve your grades. I misunderstood just now, but I still think consulting your cram school teacher might be a good idea, as they probably know your current situation best. What do you think?

dialogue.content: もちろん塾ではちゃんと先生に相談してます。カリキュラムも組んでもらってやってます。
dialogue.English: Of course, I do consult with my teacher at the cram school. They've even set up a curriculum for me, and I'm following it.

dialogue.content: だけど、勉強できないから困っているんです
dialogue.English: But I'm still struggling because I can't study effectively.

dialogue.content: 相談もされていたんですね、それでも勉強できない、、お母さんの見張りがストレスになっているのかと感じましたがいかがですか？
dialogue.English: So you have been consulting them, and even so, you're struggling to study... I'm wondering if your mother’s monitoring is a source of stress. How does that sound to you?

dialogue.content: ストレスにはなっていますが、母のことより今は勉強のことを何とかしたいです
dialogue.English: It is stressful, but right now, I want to figure out my studies more than the issue with my mother.

dialogue.content: 成績あげなきゃって色々ストレスの中頑張ってるんですよね。
dialogue.English: You’re doing your best amid all this stress, feeling like you have to raise your grades.

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: That's right.

dialogue.content: しんどいですよね、、
dialogue.English: That must be exhausting...

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 成績って上げようと思って上がるとは思わないです。オンとオフを切り替えも大事かなと。
dialogue.English: I don't think grades improve just because you want them to. I think it's also important to be able to switch between 'on' and 'off' time.

dialogue.content: 今年、受験なのであげないと困るんです
dialogue.English: I have entrance exams this year, so if I don't improve them, I'll be in trouble.

dialogue.content: そうですね、勿論受験だから、気持ち焦りますよね。少し質問いいですか？よく寝れてますか？
dialogue.English: Right, with entrance exams, it’s natural to feel anxious. May I ask a quick question? Are you sleeping well?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 寝れていたら良かったです。楽しい事をほんの少しでも取り入れて欲しいなと思ったのですが、何か興味のある事や好きな事を短い時間で出来る事あったら。気分転換って大事ですよね。
dialogue.English: I'm glad to hear you're sleeping well. I was thinking it would be good for you to incorporate even a little bit of fun into your routine. Is there anything you're interested in or enjoy that you can do for a short time? Taking a break to refresh your mind is important.

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: I suppose so.

dialogue.content: 楽しいの後って不思議と集中力が出たりしますよ。ちなみに何が出来そうですか？
dialogue.English: It's strange, but you often find you can concentrate better after you've had some fun. For instance, what do you think you could do?

dialogue.content: 今はおもいつかないです
dialogue.English: I can't think of anything right now.

dialogue.content: 好きな俳優のドラマ少しだけでも見るとか、お母さんがうるさかったらイヤホンで音楽聞くとか、雑誌みるとか、好きな料理作るとか・・
dialogue.English: Like watching a bit of a drama with your favorite actor, or if your mother is nagging, listening to music with earphones, reading a magazine, making your favorite dish...

dialogue.content: 勉強しないでそんなことしたら、また怒られます
dialogue.English: If I do something like that instead of studying, I'll just get yelled at again.

dialogue.content: そうですね、長い時間は良くないかもですが、勉強も心に余裕が無いと入らないかと思うのです。ほんの少しの時間でも神田さんの心がホッとして、勉強に集中する切り替えが出来たら、お母さんにこれが必要なんだって言えたらいいなと思いました。が出来る事からでいいので・・
dialogue.English: You're right, a long time might not be good, but I think it's hard for information to sink in when you don't have any mental breathing room. I was thinking it would be great if you could find even a short amount of time for your mind to feel at ease, to switch gears and focus on your studies, and then maybe you could even tell your mother that this is something you need. But just start with what you can do...

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Okay.

dialogue.content: 時間になってしまいました。切り替え是非やってみて下さいね。受験応援しています。
dialogue.English: It looks like our time is up. Please do try to switch gears like we talked about. I'm rooting for you with your exams.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you for your time.

dialogue.content: 終了ボタンをおしますね。
dialogue.English: I'll press the end button now.

dialogue.content: （お疲れさまでした。ありがとうございました）
dialogue.English: (Thank you for your time. I appreciate it.)
